en: Know what every candle, soap and balm costs and what to charge
Formula costing, batch costs and pricing for candle, soap and body-care makers
Batch cost sheet with the gap to standard
every batch shows its cost per good unit against the standard cost of the product, so a batch that used too much wax or too many hours is flagged the same day
Full cost per unit with overhead and packaging
materials, labour minutes, the overhead per unit and the packaging add up to the cost that a price has to cover, for all 24 products
Margin after channel fee and shipping
each product and channel shows the fee, the shipping you absorb and the margin left, with the lowest price that keeps your minimum margin
Fragrance load check on every batch
wax and fragrance weights give the load (fragrance weight as a share of wax weight), the gap to the target and the fragrance cost of the batch
oil weights, the factors from your own supplier sheet, a discount and a water ratio give the lye and water in grams as plain arithmetic, never a recipe claim
components, box, tissue and assembly minutes give the cost of a set, the price for your margin and the saving the customer sees against buying the parts
a new cost per kilogram becomes a cost per unit, a lower margin and the price rise needed, before you decide to raise a price or to absorb it
the courier cost, the shipping you charge and your margin give the order value where free shipping still pays, next to the amount you use now
a discount shows the margin after it, the profit lost on each sale and the extra units you must sell to earn the same profit
Minimum price and break-even by product
the lowest price with no loss, the lowest price for your minimum margin and the units a month that cover your fixed costs
Price tests with the profit change
units before and during a test at a new price give the unit change and the change in profit, so a price rise that cost more sales than it earned is visible
Shipping bands against the courier cost
each method and weight band compares the price you charge with the courier cost and marks the bands that lose money

Batch records, cure dates, yield and quality checks for candle and soap makers
Batch record with batch number and lots
each batch has its number, maker, units, issue, quality result and the lots of wax, oil and fragrance, so a problem is traced to a day and a delivery
each batch on a shelf shows its ready date, the days left and whether it was released on time, so nothing is sold early or forgotten
the hours of every maker on every planned day are added up and flagged against your limit, so a day with five batches shows before it happens
good units as a share of planned units for each product over 90 days, with the waste cost and the gap to the target of the product
Quality check log with weight tolerance
each weight check shows the gap in grams and percent against your tolerance, so a unit that is too light or too heavy is a recheck, not a surprise
each batch records the label version and whether ingredients and warnings are printed, with a stop for the packer (check your own local rules)
a unit kept from each batch with its box and check date, and the samples due for a check shown in red
service every number of days for 14 tools, with the next date, the days left and the items overdue
the forecast units of the core products become the batches to start, with the units sold against the forecast
units remade, relabelled or sold as seconds with their value, so the cost of fixing mistakes is a number and not a feeling
Lot trace from batch to material
each lot used in a batch with the quantity and value, so one bad delivery shows every batch it went into
batches and hours of each maker for 16 weeks against the hours they can give, with the weeks over capacity flagged

Open Start and type your company name and your own numbers in the yellow cells: your lowest margin, the margin you want, the minimum order, the grace days for an invoice, the late fee and the yearly cost of waiting for money.

Wholesale accounts lists the shops you sell to (selling to shops at about half the retail price) with the terms, the tier and the minimum order. The orders, sales, last order, usual gap, open invoices and reorder check fill in.

Wholesale orders and Wholesale lines hold each order and its products. The total, the cost of goods, the margin (profit as a share of the price) and the minimum check fill in, and the maker and the packer get a ready message.

Wholesale invoices and Payments received follow the money. Only open invoices turn late, after the grace days; the days to pay and the oldest late invoice are on the dashboard. Credit notes and Returns and credits record what you gave back.

Line sheet is the price and product list you give a shop, with the wholesale price, the retail price, the minimum pack and the margin for the shop. Price tiers and Terms options hold the discounts and the early payment discount.
Sample requests, Shop calls and visits, Account notes, Prospects and Catalogue requests keep the selling work: what you sent, who you talked to, what the shop said and which prospect is next.

Reorder reminders turns the usual gap between orders into the next expected order of each shop and product, so you call before a shop forgets you. Account sales by month gives the sales and the margin of each shop.
Wholesale shipments records the boxes, the weight, the courier cost and the days to deliver, and shows the freight as a share of the order.
